title: Contrary & Protected Dragon — Dual-Mega Field Manual
lede: Staraptor scales through Contrary while Farigiraf amplifies Garchomp-Z; Gold and Milotic keep both branches alive.
philosophy: Choose one Mega win condition at preview. Staraptor spends Charm and Close Combat on physical durability; Garchomp-Z spends natural Speed and Helping Hand on immediate special damage. Farigiraf denies opposing priority and reverses room, Whimsicott controls speed and Attack, Milotic sustains, and Gholdengo converts a failed primary route into a second win condition. The best four are those whose support resources actually work together.
meta: Pokemon Champions Regulation M-C; proposed experimental registered six as of 2026-09-25, no measured win rate.

Garchomp attacks before many unboosted opponents without requiring Tailwind. Target a check to the future Gholdengo endgame or a Pokémon able to remove Farigiraf. engines.how: Whimsicott gives Staraptor Attack without using the attacker’s move, and the following Close Combat grants permanent-on-field defensive boosts through Contrary. A first exchange can therefore manufacture both damage and durability. Roost retains boosts by keeping Staraptor active while recovering Brave Bird recoil. Against an immediate knockout threat, Tailwind or Protect is more appropriate than blind Charm. A Ghost or dangerous special attacker can interrupt the chain, so Gholdengo and Milotic must be used before Staraptor is forced to make a losing attack.

engines.how: This team is naturally fast in Mega Garchomp-Z mode but still requires answers to opponent-created speed states. Whimsicott gives all active and future teammates a finite Tailwind window; Milotic can change a particular opposing Pokémon’s order more persistently. Farigiraf is primarily an anti-room tool rather than a dedicated hard-room engine. Select the control action that lets an attacker actually secure progress on the following exchange. Blindly clicking Trick Room while bringing two fast attackers may benefit the opponent instead.

Icy Wind helps both Mega branches and Gholdengo, while Scald may lower incoming physical pressure via burn. counters.why: Staraptor and Milotic can share Electric vulnerability and Staraptor must survive before scaling.

counters.name: Strong spread attacks
counters.why: Armor Tail is not Wide Guard and there is no redirection on the registered six.

counters.name: Dark attackers into Farigiraf and Gold
counters.why: Farigiraf weak to Dark, Gold weak to Dark, so position carefully.

advantages.title: Two Mega roots
advantages.body: One roster creates a Staraptor physical scaling mode and a Garchomp-Z immediate special mode.

advantages.title: Portable defensive resources
advantages.body: Leftovers Milotic and Farigiraf do not need weather or terrain to activate.

advantages.title: Independent Gold
advantages.body: Nasty Plot and Make It Rain remain an alternate route when the Mega is countered.

hazards.title: Only one Mega
hazards.body: Both stones may be registered and selected among four, but only one can Mega Evolve per battle.

hazards.title: Base-form tax
hazards.body: Special Timid Garchomp with Z stone is weaker without Mega; base Staraptor lacks Contrary.

hazards.title: No Fake Out, Wide Guard, redirection or terrain
hazards.body: Do not claim Armor Tail stops ordinary attacks or spread damage.

hazards.title: Prankster interactions
hazards.body: Psychic Terrain can block priority against grounded opposing targets; Dark targets may block opposing Prankster moves. Allied Charm still targets your own Mega Staraptor.

matchupScripts.name: Fake Out / Sucker Punch priority
matchupScripts.why: Armor Tail protects fast converter actions.

matchupScripts.name: Intimidate physical balance
matchupScripts.why: Contrary and Competitive punish stat drops.

matchupScripts.name: Dedicated Trick Room
matchupScripts.why: Preserve Farigiraf to reverse an active room.

matchupScripts.name: Fast Tailwind offense
matchupScripts.why: Tailwind helps Garchomp and Gold compete with faster state.

matchupScripts.name: Fairy / Ghost defensive pivot
matchupScripts.why: Gold can act as first-wave attacker.

matchupScripts.name: Repeated physical damage / long games
matchupScripts.why: Milotic and Farigiraf preserve Staraptor scaling.

rejectedAlts: Base Raichu support without Mega was not retained because of offensive slot cost.

Test Farigiraf Psychic versus Twin Beam or Thunderbolt if rain leads dominate.
Test Garchomp physical Ground move/mixed SP only if dual-stone packages are selected frequently.
Evaluate whether no Wide Guard is an unacceptable spread weakness.

phases.title: Preview
phases.body: Name chosen Mega, lead target, opposing speed state, and second win condition.

phases.title: First exchange
phases.body: Immediate Helping Hand damage or Charm-to-Close Combat, unless survival requires Protect or Tailwind.

phases.title: Midgame
phases.body: Use Gold and Milotic to answer counters without donating a turn.

phases.title: Endgame
phases.body: Stop setup; spend remaining health, speed and damage on decisive attacks.

loops.title: Priority-protected Dragon
loops.body: If Garchomp already outspeeds the decisive target, Farigiraf Helping Hands and Garchomp attacks immediately.

loops.title: Contrary defense engine
loops.body: If Staraptor survives its first action, allied Charm boosts Attack and Close Combat boosts both defenses.

loops.title: Gold fallback
loops.body: If the Mega draws a counter, preserve it and transfer damage to Gholdengo.

speedRegimes.label: Garchomp-Z natural fast mode
speedRegimes.creates: High innate Speed without a setter
speedRegimes.expiresInto: Only changes when mega state or opposing control changes.

speedRegimes.label: Whimsicott Tailwind
speedRegimes.expiresInto: Native Speed; plan attacks before it ends.

speedRegimes.label: Milotic Icy Wind
speedRegimes.expiresInto: Target may switch to reset reductions.

speedRegimes.label: Farigiraf Trick Room reversal
speedRegimes.window: Use after opponent has established room.

pairChemistries.label: Protected Dragon
diesTo: Ordinary spread or strong Dark attack into Farigiraf
pairChemistries.secondWave: Gold for Fairy/Ghost, Milotic for Speed.

pairChemistries.label: Contrary acceleration
pairChemistries.secondWave: Gold on Ghost/Fairy checks; Milotic on long trades.

pairChemistries.label: Protected physical attack
diesTo: Ordinary special burst and spread damage
pairChemistries.secondWave: Whimsicott for delayed Charm; Gold for defensive counters.

pairChemistries.label: Amplified Gold first wave
diesTo: Wide Guard on Make It Rain
pairChemistries.secondWave: Garchomp for Ground coverage, Milotic for Speed.

evidence.source: User team decisions plus prior conversation; external move and mechanic references checked for Farigiraf, Staraptor and Milotic.
evidence.caveat: Proposed team and packages, not an observed Master-rank team or experimentally measured win rate. SP spreads are starting points, not simulated benchmarks. Catalog slug for new Mega Garchomp-Z requires verification against the deployed Ringside species catalog.
